item.title: USS Washington aircraft carrier heads to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln
item.description: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed Vietnam last week and is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Golfer Jessica Bang, 18, dies while preparing for tournament in Thailand
item.description: Jessica Bang collapsed on Aug. 1 as she was preparing in Thailand for a tournament and was transported to a hospital in Bangkok.

item.title: Marine vet on USS Lincoln's 200+ days without port call: "Very abnormal number"
item.description: Jonathan Simkins, editor-in-chief of the Military Times and a Marine Corps veteran, joins CBS News 24/7 to share his thoughts on the reports of poor conditions on the ship and the crew's record-setting deployment.

item.title: Paintings worth $10 million that were stolen in 3-minute heist are recovered
item.description: The recovered works are valued at more than $10 million.

item.title: Can taking weight-loss drugs help you get hired? Yes, if you're a woman.
item.description: Going on GLP-1 drugs significantly boosted unemployed women's chances of finding a job, according to a Harvard economist.

item.title: Feds charge woman for allegedly vandalizing World War II Memorial in D.C.
item.description: The top federal prosecutor in Washington, D.C., said a woman has been arrested and faces two felony charges related to vandalism of the World War II Memorial.

item.title: How double jeopardy could come into play after Mangione guilty plea
item.description: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to two federal counts on Friday. His state trial is currently scheduled to begin on Sept. 8.

item.title: Trump says U.S. warship's 9-month deployment "not nearly long enough"
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for almost nine months and is expected to be replaced in the Middle East.

item.title: How to get a refund for Trump tariffs struck down by Supreme Court
item.description: The U.S. has refunded more than $100 billion in illegal tariffs to businesses, and some of that money is going to consumers — here's what to know.

item.title: Watch: Trump says USS Lincoln is being replaced, doesn't think deployment has been too long
item.description: President Trump responded Friday to a question about the USS Abraham Lincoln, denying reports of bad conditions and saying the ship's deployment hasn't been "nearly long enough."

item.title: Watch rescue workers save people and pets in the aftermath of Colombia earthquake
item.description: A deadly 7.4 magnitude earthquake rocked Colombia, destroying homes and devastating communities. Watch rescuers pull survivors from the wreckage, bringing moments of hope as the country recovers from the disaster.

item.title: American missionary released after kidnapping 9 months ago in Niger, organization says
item.description: Kevin Rideout, an American missionary who was kidnapped in the West African nation of Niger in October, has been released, President Trump and Rideout's organization said Friday. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: What Luigi Mangione said as he pleaded guilty to killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione on Friday entered a guilty plea in his federal case, admitting he shot and killed UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside a Midtown Manhattan hotel in 2024. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman and Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: Violent crime plummeted in U.S. last year, White House official says
item.description: The White House is touting a historic drop in violent crime as the FBI prepares to release the latest data from its annual Uniform Crime Reporting Program.

item.title: Walmart tomato soup kits recalled over Listeria risk, FDA says
item.description: The 14oz soup kits were distributed at Walmart stores in 29 states between June 30 and July 7, according to the FDA.

item.title: Hawaii under a hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala takes aim
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring heavy rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands as a hurricane this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: Count Binface wins hearts, if not the election, in bid to defeat Trump ally
item.description: Count Binface, a satirical candidate who's become a mainstay in recent U.K. elections, achieved his greatest success yet.

item.title: Warship that sank in 1908 found off U.K.: "Undisturbed for 118 years"
item.description: The Royal Navy and shipwreck hunters have been searching in vain for the remains of HMS Tiger for over a century.

item.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case, admits shooting Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione entered a guilty plea in his federal case at a court appearance in Manhattan Friday morning.

item.title: Brian Thompson's family reacts after Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case
item.description: The family of slain UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson is reacting to news that his alleged killer, Luigi Mangione, plans to plead guilty in the federal case against him. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Inside "the Pool": Fugitive arrested in alleged cross-border car trade scheme
item.description: Along the Texas-Mexico border, prosecutors say a group of businessmen found a way to monopolize the trade of used cars — a scheme called "the Pool." This week, authorities say they caught one alleged member.

item.title: Officials react to Luigi Mangione's guilty plea in federal case
item.description: United States Attorney Jamie McDonald and New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch spoke to reporters after a court hearing where Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in the federal case against him for the death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Katrina Kaufman and Tom Hanson have more.

item.title: Luigi Mangione's lawyer speaks out after he announced guilty plea in federal case
item.description: Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Luigi Mangione's attorney, spoke to reporters outside a New York City federal court, where he told a judge that he would plead guilty in his federal case. CBS News' Tom Hanson and Katrina Kaufman report.

item.title: Indiana river breaks 1913 flooding record as governor declares state of emergency
item.description: The White River in Indiana rose to record-breaking levels as more than 11 inches of rain has fallen east of Indianapolis since Tuesday.

item.title: See how much renters pay for a 2-bedroom home in 50 U.S. cities
item.description: Nearly half of renters spend more than 30% of their income on housing. Here's what it costs to rent a two-bedroom home in 50 U.S. cities.

item.title: 2 killed as Apache helicopter from Fort Hood crashes in Salado, Texas
item.description: Two soldiers aboard an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based out of Fort Hood were killed in a crash on Wednesday, according to local authorities and the Army.

item.title: Treating Lindsay Clancy | Case by Case | "48 Hours" Podcast
item.description: The focus in the Lindsay Clancy trial shifts to her mental health treatment as jurors hear testimony from her psychiatric providers, friends, and family. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty and CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul break down the emotional moments in court, the competing narratives emerging at the center of the case, and the lasting questions surrounding maternal mental health.

item.title: My husband was kicked out of hospice. Here's what I learned.
item.description: Some seriously ill patients improve on hospice. About 1 in 16 patients enrolled in hospice care lose eligibility as a result. Here's how to get appropriate care.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite perform "I Can't Hold Out"
item.description: Grammy-winning harmonica virtuoso Charlie Musselwhite is a pioneer of the 60s Chicago blues scene. New England blues trio GA-20 is celebrated for their raucous sound and dynamic live performances. GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite join forces for an electrifying blues collaboration, culminating in their new album "Blues Now!"
